A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same higher-order convolution study. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, relocated, and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original texture-classification and image-benchmark experiments, architectural ablations, perturbation tests, and representation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds ImageNet, fine-grained bird classification, corruption robustness, computational benchmarking, and ResNet scaling results.

M1.justification: The Volterra-style convolution, independent weights across orders, normalization, and early-layer higher-order blocks are retained. The additional ResNet evaluations apply the existing approach to different model configurations; no new higher-order operator, objective, or inference procedure is documented.

E1.justification: v2 adds full ImageNet, CUB-200-2011 fine-grained bird classification, and common-corruption scenarios on CIFAR-10-C and CIFAR-100-C. The original synthetic textures, MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR datasets, and Imagenette remain. Imagenette moves to Appendix A.6 rather than being removed.

E2.justification: v2 Table 4 adds ResNet-18/34/50 comparisons on the four smaller benchmarks, substantially expanding experiments previously centered on shallow CNNs and a deeper plain CNN. The existing Imagenette comparisons with ResNet-18 and VOneNet are retained. The expanded discussion of prior Volterra methods does not introduce empirical comparisons against those methods.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include a FLOP-controlled CIFAR-10 comparison, ResNet depth scaling, and normalized corruption accuracy, with severity-1 results tabulated. ImageNet and CUB introduce additional training protocols; CUB specifies 224-pixel inputs, augmented training, momentum SGD, cosine scheduling, and 100 epochs. These supplement the retained small-benchmark and Imagenette settings.

E4.justification: Appendices A.2, A.4, A.5, and A.8 add computational profiling and FLOP controls, depth-scaling analysis, common-corruption robustness tests, and qualitative bird-classification error analysis. Earlier placement, kernel-size, nonlinearity, targeted-perturbation, and representation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 specifies five independent ImageNet runs with mean and standard deviation and explicitly identifies CUB results as single-run. Table 2 now distinguishes benchmark-specific run counts. The original 50-run small-benchmark protocol and single-run Imagenette status remain; the latter was already disclosed in v1 Appendix A.3. No specified significance test or confidence-interval procedure is added.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and perturbation scores are retained. New results include ImageNet accuracy of 69.47 ± 0.09% for HoResNet-18 versus 68.62 ± 0.08% for ResNet-18, and CUB accuracy of 72.31% versus 68.24%. Tables 3–6 additionally report FLOP-controlled performance, ResNet scaling, and corruption outcomes. These are added experimental results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The polynomial formulations, tied-weight expansion, symmetry-based parameter formula, normalization, and asymptotic complexity expressions are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. v2's numerical symmetry savings and FLOP measurements add implementation and computational evidence rather than new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central claims about higher-order convolution, optimal third/fourth-order expansions, and distinctive representations remain. The novelty claim is qualified: v1 emphasizes fundamentally differing through embedding higher-order operations inside convolution, whereas v2 acknowledges extending and complementing earlier Volterra approaches and emphasizes higher-order analysis and mechanistic insights.

C2.justification: v1 already acknowledges computational overhead and sensitivity to targeted perturbations. v2 develops quantitative computation and memory limitations, distinguishes targeted statistical sensitivity from common-corruption robustness, interprets depth scaling and fine-grained results, and discusses possible complementarity with attention. Sections 5.1–5.2 substantially expand applicability boundaries and future directions.

D1.justification: v1 promises code release upon publication; v2 Appendix A.1 supplies a code-repository link. v2 also documents GPU types, training-time estimates, concrete symmetry savings, and detailed CUB optimization, augmentation, and training-budget information. These materially improve the documented reproduction path, although the repository itself was not inspected.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 substantially revises positioning relative to Zoumpourlis and Roheda, adds Li et al.'s Volterra-convolution work, and distinguishes contributions through expansion order and analysis. Section 5.2 adds substantive comparison with Vision Transformers. Dataset and corruption references are added, while several biological and adversarial-analysis citations are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract is substantially compressed, biological motivation and related work are rewritten, and the discussion is reorganized into limitations and future directions. Imagenette moves from the main experiments to the appendix, supplementary sections are reorganized, and a NeurIPS checklist is added. These changes substantially revise the narrative and document structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains a texture inset, Figure 3 simplifies the full-network diagrams into block comparisons, and Figure 4 removes its distance-distribution panel while that analysis remains in Figure 11. New tables display computational, scaling, corruption, and CUB results; Imagenette receives a separate appendix table. The document also adopts a different conference layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited evidence for large-scale applicability and computational fairness through five-run ImageNet evaluation, deeper-network comparisons, and FLOP controls. Corruption tests, more precise novelty positioning, explicit limitations, and documented code access further strengthen assessment and reproducibility. Single-run CUB results and unexplained uncertainty terms in Tables 5–6 limit some additions, but the expanded validation and transparency provide a substantial overall quality gain.
